set.st: June 1905: a stranger from Indiana boarded with the farmer and, with his leave, dug numerous holes in the grove near an old house long said to be haunted, after about $15,000 thought cached in early days by thieves; an old settler said the neighbourhood was once a rendezvous for horse thieves running between northern Iowa and Hastings. He found nothing and left. Private farmland: permission. Pin is the Philbrook quarter (1896 atlas), not the spot itself. The old settler thought the digger was the gang's agent or had been set on by their tale. The digger carried a railroad pass. The New Richland Star (22 Jun 1905) says the stranger, 'a man of spiritualistic proclivities', got leave from Mr. Heckes, 'who owns the Philbrook farm', to dig in the grove near the old house, long reputed haunted; after several visits and 'numerous holes about the premises' he gave up, denying that a fortune teller had sent him. Nothing found.
